f2_source_observed.wp206_observation: Recovery validates canonical DB file identity, checkpoint digest/typed replay, one-per-checkpoint recovery state and compare-and-swap. recovery_provenance_ref is caller-supplied text; recovery_id hashes that text but no content/object behind the reference is authenticated at this boundary.
f2_source_observed.wp206_g4_test_observation: G4 proves exact repeat with the same provenance string and rejects a conflicting provenance string; the test provenance values are opaque literals and do not authenticate referenced evidence content.
f2_source_observed.wp901_g3_observation: Current F2 already has a typed source-binding pattern that derives principal IDs/digests from concrete source objects and a CausalIdentity rather than accepting a parallel caller-controlled expected identity set; it explicitly does not claim persisted-row attestation.

external_primary_sources.relevance: Attestation statements bind predicates to explicit subjects/resources by digest; supports content-addressed evidence-subject identity rather than opaque reference identity.
Provenance is a verifiable relationship between a produced subject and its origin/build context; supports exact subject binding but is broader than WP206 needs.
Signed bundles combine signature and verification material when producer authenticity is part of the threat model; this is stronger and operationally heavier than local content binding.

Persisted trusted metadata and monotone versions provide rollback protection; useful analogy, but WP206 already has unique one-time recovery plus CAS and does not justify importing TUF semantics by default.

hypothesis: WP206 G4 closes repeat-provenance substitution only at opaque-reference-string identity. A mutable, aliased or otherwise unauthenticated evidence target can retain the same reference string while its content changes, leaving an evidence-subject binding gap.
counterhypothesis: No further binding is needed because one-per-checkpoint recovery, exact checkpoint/receipt checks and CAS already prevent a second recovery and therefore provenance content cannot affect canonical state after the first transition.
source_discriminator_result: COUNTERHYPOTHESIS_PARTIALLY_REJECTED_AT_E1: current WP206 controls protect the state transition and repeat semantics, but they do not establish what external evidence the first recovery provenance string actually denotes. This is an evidence-authentication gap, not a demonstrated state-transition corruption bug.
minimality_result: Do not import Sigstore, Rekor, TUF or a second provenance database for this gap. The smallest supported direction is a typed/content-addressed recovery evidence subject, preferably reusing F2's existing WP901 G3 typed-source/CausalIdentity pattern. Cryptographic producer authentication remains a separate later threat-model gate only if recovery callers/evidence producers are not trusted.

efficiency.typed_local_subject_digest: constant-size typed data/hash; no model call; no network; negligible steady-state overhead
efficiency.sigstore_tuf_stack: additional trust roots, verification logic/dependencies and possibly network/log operations; not justified by current E1 evidence
